newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close easier after roller-coaster ride.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close easier after roller-coaster ride.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed slightly lower on Wednesday after a day of big price swings as profit-taking alternated with bargain-hunting, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index ended 18.19 points, or 0.13 percent, lower at 14,421.52 after moving between 14,213.95 and 14,575.16.
Turnover was HK$17.51 billion, down from Tuesday's HK$20.91 billion.

"The market is overhung by fears that the government will introduce new measures to rein in speculation on the property market. Also, Hong Kong stocks have risen too sharply lately," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
But Hong Kong's handover to China at midnight on June 30 was considered positive news by the market and should give the blue-chip index some support, Au said.
Follow-through selling on property stocks and utilities spilled over from Tuesday to drag down the Hang Seng to near the 14,200 level before the index rebounded in early afternoon.
"The market is choppy today, just like a roller-coaster," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
He said sentiment turned slightly bearish on concerns over anti-speculation measures in the property market. Only banks and a few blue-chip laggards benefited from rallies overseas.
HSBC Holdings added HK$3.00 to HK$233.00 and Hang Seng Bank rose HK$1.50 to HK$90.75, while Cheung Kong slipped HK$1.00 to HK$74.00 and Henderson Land lost HK$1.25 at HK$68.25.
Brokers said continued profit-taking was seen on red chips in the midst of Beijing's most recent drive to halt speculative trading on China's stock markets.
The Yamaichi Red Chip Index, complied by Yamaichi International, eased 2.8 percent to 2,739.8. "The index has fallen about 7.5 percent in last three trading days," Tang said.
Beijing Enterprises eased HK$1.20 to HK$45.80.
China Everbright Technology plunged HK$0.28 to HK$1.56 and China Resources fell HK$1.50 to HK$25.10.
But Shanghai Industrial edged up HK$0.40 to HK$41.90.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index for the 28 H-shares dropped 30.93 points, or three percent, to 1,001.54.

Sentiment was hit by news that two senior officials at H-share company Guangshen Railway had been relieved of their duties over allegations of improper investments, brokers said. The stock slid HK$0.375, or 10.5 percent, to HK$3.20.
